hypothesis: If the Glacial period lasted a very long time at each place and was at least in part simultaneous across the whole world, then (a) a globally mixed marine proxy of ice volume and deep-water temperature (benthic d18O) shows prolonged cold, ice-rich states lasting well over 10 thousand years and recurring through the Pleistocene, with the last glacial maximum in such a state, and (b) a southern-hemisphere high-latitude temperature record (Antarctic ice core) is cold at the same times as the global proxy is ice-rich, within age-model uncertainty.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Data: (1) LR04 benthic d18O stack of Lisiecki and Raymo (2005), the LR04stack.txt file served by the author (columns: age in ka, benthic d18O in per mil, error), and (2) EPICA Dome C deuterium-derived temperature anomaly on the EDC3 age scale (Jouzel et al. 2007), the NOAA paleoclimatology file edc3deuttemp2007.txt. Criterion A (long-lasting cold states): with d18O linearly interpolated to a 1-kyr grid over 0-2600 ka, d18O >= 4.0 per mil during at least 20% of the interval AND at least 5 separate contiguous intervals with d18O >= 4.0 per mil each lasting >= 10 kyr. Criterion B (last glacial maximum): mean d18O over 18-26 ka >= 4.5 per mil. Criterion C (simultaneity, north-dominated ice volume vs southern temperature): both series interpolated to a 1-kyr grid over 0-800 ka; the maximum Pearson correlation between EDC temperature anomaly and negative d18O across lags of -6 to +6 kyr (to allow for independent age models) is >= 0.6. SUPPORTS if A, B and C all hold.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. REFUTES if d18O >= 4.0 per mil covers < 10% of 0-2600 ka, OR fewer than 2 contiguous >= 4.0 per mil intervals last >= 10 kyr, OR the 18-26 ka mean d18O is < 4.2 per mil, OR the maximum lagged correlation in criterion C is < 0.3 (southern temperature not in step with global ice volume). MIXED otherwise (values between the support and refute thresholds, or A and B holding while C is between 0.3 and 0.6). INCONCLUSIVE (data-unavailable) if either file cannot be downloaded.
interpretation: Darwin's Glacial period is mapped to the Pleistocene glacial stages. 'Lasted a very long time' is read as cold states of at least 10 kyr; 'simultaneous across the whole world' is read as the Antarctic (southern high-latitude) temperature record being in step with the benthic d18O stack, whose glacial signal is dominated by northern-hemisphere ice sheets; this is a two-hemisphere test of simultaneity at the resolution of orbital cycles, not of the sub-millennial bipolar seesaw. Darwin implied one long glacial episode; the data show many cycles, so the test asks whether long, globally cold intervals recur and co-occur. The 4.0 and 4.5 per mil thresholds and the 0.6 correlation threshold were fixed before any data were read. Criteria A and B follow the swarm thread's draft plan; criterion C was added to address the simultaneity clause the draft could not test.
